newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly lower, quiet due to holida.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly lower, quiet due to holida.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly lower on Friday but trading was thin due to the All Saints' holiday, traders said.
Gas oil business was quiet due to holidays in much of Europe and heating oil requirements for early November well covered.

Outright outright prices slid $7 in sympathy with IPE futures but premiums were seen slightly stronger, and traders said further declines on the screen could open an arbitrage opportunities to Asia for certain Russian grades.
One player assessed Russian basis Genoa at a bid of around high cif +$1.50 with an offer at +$2.50, around 50 cents firmer.
Another trader suggested Russian premiums at cif high +$1.50/2.0 compared to +$1/1.50 earlier in the week.
Buying interest was scarce for low sulphur diesel and one company with cargoes on offer said buyers were.
Naphtha prices drifted lower with yesterday's sharp selloff in crude and gasoline, but most business was wrapped up before today because of the All Saints' holiday.
Traders said high freight costs were still discouraging shipping cargoes to northwest Europe from the Med.
Gasoline prices also bounced back from earlier losses after crude and gasoline futures stabilised.
One trader said Italy's market appeared fairly balanced for now.
Fuel oil markets were similarly becalmed. Russian supply out of the Black Sea appears to be drying up as winter deepens.

One dealer said he thought a large trader had won at least part of Turkey's latest tender for 25,000-50,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil, as well as part of the tender for 55,000-60,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil.
